blocks.name: todo-calendar
blocks.title: To-do Calendar
blocks.description: A weekly to-do card whose active week expands into a compact month calendar.
blocks.lede: Keeps the selected date, its agenda, and nearby days together while a seven-day strip morphs into a complete month.
blocks.installation: Installs the To-do Calendar block with Button, Icon Morph, Morphing Text, and shared motion foundations.
guidance: Use this block when a date picker also needs to expose tasks or deadlines for the selected day.
Keep item titles short enough to scan and use descriptions only for useful context.
Use the Calendar primitive when the interface only needs date selection.
behavior: The collapsed state shows the selected week and task markers for all seven days.
Opening the calendar keeps the active week alive while surrounding weeks expand around it; a second-week strip therefore moves into the second calendar row.
Agenda items appear between the selected-date header and the week or month surface.
Date, hover, and selection indicators use the shared motion tokens and respect reduced-motion preferences.
accessibility: The block exposes a labelled region, calendar grid, selected dates, and descriptive date labels.
The calendar toggle exposes its expanded state and changes its accessible name with the view.
Interactive agenda items use pressed state to communicate completion.
api: Agenda items containing id, title, date, optional description, and completion state.
Called when a day is selected.
Makes agenda rows interactive and reports the item being toggled.
Optional action rendered beside the calendar toggle, such as a Dialog with an add button trigger.
Shows the complete month on first render.
Locale used for date, month, and weekday labels.
Starts each week on Sunday or Monday.
Additional classes on the outer card.
blocks.customization: Supply application-owned items and state handlers. The card, agenda rows, date indicators, radii, and motion inherit the shared Rhoe UI theme tokens.

groups.name: Forms
groups.description: Complete form flows composed from Rhoe UI controls.

blocks.name: auth-form
blocks.title: Authentication Form
blocks.description: Sign-in and sign-up forms that morph into password recovery or email verification flows.
blocks.lede: Combines social authentication, email credentials, verification, recovery, consent, and account switching in one responsive surface.
blocks.installation: Installs the Authentication Form block with Button, Input, Checkbox, and shared Rhoe UI foundations.

examples.title: Submit form data
Sign up and verify
Four OAuth providers
examples.code:
<AuthForm
  mode="sign-in"
  oauthProviders={[github, google, microsoft, apple]}
  onSubmit={handleSignIn}
/>

examples.title: OTP password recovery
examples.code:
<AuthForm
  mode="sign-in"
  forgotPasswordVariant="otp"
  onForgotPassword={sendResetCode}
  onVerifyResetCode={verifyResetCode}
  onResetPassword={resetPassword}
  onSubmit={handleSignIn}
/>

examples.title: Show verification errors
examples.code:
<AuthForm
  mode="sign-up"
  signUpVerificationVariant="otp"
  onSubmit={handleSignUp}
  onVerifyCode={async (code, email) => {
    const response = await fetch("/api/auth/verify", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ code, email }),
    })

    if (!response.ok) return { error: "That code is invalid or has expired." }
  }}
/>

examples.title: Application-owned recovery
examples.description: The default variant does not prescribe what happens after submission.
examples.code:
<AuthForm
  mode="sign-in"
  onSubmit={handleSignIn}
  onForgotPassword={async (email) => {
    // Redirect, open a dialog, start passkey recovery, or use any custom flow.
    await startCustomRecovery(email)
  }}
/>

guidance: Use one to four OAuth providers. The block automatically arranges them as 1, 2, 2 + 1, or 2 x 2.
Connect OAuth buttons and every async callback to application-owned authentication routes.
Return { error: message } from an async callback to show a specific error, or false for a generic error. Invalid verification codes appear on the OTP field.
Return false from sign-up onSubmit when account creation fails so the credentials form stays open.
Use the default variant for an application-owned continuation such as routing, dialogs, magic links, passkeys, security questions, or another custom recovery flow.
Use link for the built-in check-email confirmation or OTP for built-in code verification and password replacement.
Sign-up also defaults to an application-owned continuation; choose its link or OTP preset only when needed.
Keep terms, privacy, and account-switching destinations explicit.
behavior: Every OAuth and submit button overrides the Button default width with w-full inside the block.
A single OAuth button spans one row; two share a row; the third spans the next row; four form two equal rows.
Sign-in includes email, password, and remember-device controls; recovery keeps the email and submit button as shared elements while OAuth and password controls morph away.

The shared submit button morphs through idle and pending labels including Sign in, Signing in, Sign up, Signing up, Send reset link, Sending reset link, Send OTP, Sending OTP, Verify code, Verifying code, Reset password, and Resetting password.
In OTP recovery, the email field morphs into Verification Code and then into new-password and confirmation fields.
In link recovery, a successful request morphs into Check your email and the shared action becomes Resend reset link.
Default sign-up delegates continuation to onSubmit; its link and OTP presets morph only after onSubmit resolves successfully.
Sign-up OTP keeps the email field and submit button as shared elements while they morph into Verification Code and Verify code.
Sign-up link morphs into Check your email while the shared action becomes Resend verification link.
Every OTP screen starts a configurable resend countdown and disables resend until it reaches zero.
Failed callbacks display an error; a failed OTP verification marks the code field invalid, and failed resend requests do not restart the countdown.
Password recovery checks that the new password and confirmation match before calling onResetPassword.
The surface animates its measured height while outgoing and incoming content meet at the center without scaling its fields.
Only the first four OAuth providers are rendered.
accessibility: The block uses a semantic form with native email, password, required, autocomplete, and submit behavior.
Password visibility, checkboxes, focus rings, labels, and disabled states inherit accessible Rhoe UI primitives.
After a morph, focus moves to the first available control and the changing header is announced.
The verification input uses numeric input and one-time-code autocomplete.
api: Selects the fields, copy, consent, and submit label.
Up to four provider buttons containing label, optional icon, disabled state, and click handler.
Overrides the heading or supporting copy.
Content for the internal trigger that opens password recovery beside the sign-in password label.
Optional links or actions shown in required sign-up consent; omitted props remain visible as plain text.
Sign-up or sign-in action displayed below the form.
Receives credentials. Default continuation is application-owned; link and OTP presets advance after a successful result. Return false to keep credentials visible.
Return false for a generic error, { error: message } for a specific error, or true / void for success.
Default delegates continuation to onForgotPassword; link adds a check-email confirmation and OTP adds code verification plus password replacement.
Delegates continuation to onSubmit, or uses an OTP field or check-email verification-link screen.
Countdown applied before OTP codes can be resent; set 0 to allow immediate resend.
Owns any custom continuation in the default variant, or sends the reset link or OTP for built-in variants. Return false to keep the email step open.
Verifies a recovery OTP. Return false to keep the code step open.
(password: string, confirmPassword: string, email: string) => AuthFormActionResult | Promise<AuthFormActionResult>
Submits the replacement password after a recovery OTP succeeds.
Reports credentials, sign-up verification, recovery email, link confirmation, recovery code, and reset-password transitions.
Additional classes applied to the form root.
Form attributes such as id, name, aria attributes, noValidate, method, and action are forwarded to the root form.
blocks.customization: Override title and description, provide application-owned actions, and pass one to four OAuth providers. Static layout and colors inherit the Rhoe UI Tailwind and token foundation.

groups.name: Data Visualization
groups.description: Composed data displays for live monitoring and operational views.

blocks.name: realtime-line-chart
blocks.title: Realtime Line Chart
blocks.description: A continuously advancing line chart block with a live value, optional range tabs, average, and configurable spike threshold.
blocks.lede: Keeps a fixed time window moving beneath a stationary hover reader while new measurements enter from the right.
blocks.installation: Installs Realtime Line Chart with Line Chart, Tabs, Rolling Number, Morphing Text, and shared motion foundations.

examples.title: Optional range tabs
examples.description: With one sample per second, 31, 61, and 121 samples cover 30 seconds, one minute, and two minutes. Keep enough history in metrics for the largest range. The caller updates windowSize; tabs do not filter data automatically.

guidance: Append new measurements to data instead of replacing the visible window.
Match updateInterval to the real feed cadence so motion remains continuous.
Use a stable domain to prevent the vertical scale from jumping during live updates.
Provide ranges to show grouped tabs in the header. Handle onRangeChange to update windowSize or load the matching data; omit ranges to hide the tabs.
behavior: New samples enter from the right while the existing timeline advances left at a constant speed.
The latest value uses Rolling Number. Optional range controls reuse the grouped Tabs component.
Hover remains fixed under a stationary pointer while the timeline passes beneath it.
Only the curve above spikeThreshold changes to spikeColor.
accessibility: The latest value remains readable outside the SVG.
The underlying Line Chart exposes every visible label and value to assistive technology.
Range tabs support keyboard navigation and expose the selected state.
api: Optional range choices, each with a value and label. Omit or pass an empty array to hide tabs.
Receives the selected range. Update windowSize or data in the caller.
Feed interval in milliseconds and continuous movement duration.
Threshold and curve color for spikes.
Formatting for the latest value and chart values.
Additional classes for the block root.
blocks.customization: Configure the visible window, optional grouped range tabs, feed interval, stable domain, spike threshold, and number format.
